channel.title: Filharmonia Szczecin: news
channel.description: News from the Mieczysław Karłowicz Philharmonic in Szczecin: concert previews, education, exhibitions and notices.

item.title: The Wieniawski Competition is under way, and its finalists and winners come to Szczecin in November
item.description: The 17th Henryk Wieniawski International Violin Competition is running in Poznań: 252 applicants from 36 countries, and the only Polish violinist left in round three is Zofia Anna Olesik, already known to Szczecin audiences. Results are announced on 22 October. In November we host three evenings with competition musicians: two half-recitals by participants on 13 November, then the second- and first-prize winners with the orchestra under Przemysław Neumann on 20 and 22 November, paired with further parts of Smetana’s Má vlast.

item.title: Paulina Przybysz opens the Philharmonic’s jazz series
item.description: On 19 October at 7 pm singer Paulina Przybysz starts the 2026/2027 jazz season with her project Insides. She goes back to the music she grew up with, from Ella Fitzgerald to Coltrane, and runs it through soul, hip-hop and R&B. She shares the stage with young players from the Polish jazz scene, including vibraphonist Tymon Kosma and saxophonist Olaf Węgier.

item.title: Dobrawa Czocher returns to the Philharmonic
item.description: Preview of the 16 October concert: cellist and composer Dobrawa Czocher with State of Matter, music about the sea and constant change, where her cello meets Natalia Czekała’s electronics and synths. It is a homecoming of sorts: from 2018 to 2023 she led the cello section of our orchestra.

item.title: Concert programmes go digital
item.description: Symphonic concert programmes are now digital. They usually appear the day before the concert on the event page and under Downloads, online ticket buyers get them by email, and QR codes in the foyer and at the hall doors open them on your phone. Printed programmes will only be available at selected concerts.

item.title: A week with EDUphilharmonic and a big premiere
item.description: From 10 to 19 October: ten days of concerts, workshops and meetings for children, families and schools. The highlight is the premiere of the musical show The Piano Fairy Tale (11 October, age 5+), also played for schools on 15 October. Around it: Raniutto workshops with flute, harp and Debussy for children aged 1 to 6, and a Sunday session on how the seasons sounded in the Baroque (18 October).

item.title: (NOT)Daughters: music by Irene Poldowski and Roxanna Panufnik
item.description: Preview of the 7 October chamber concert. The Poldowski String Quartet, mezzo-soprano Agata Schmidt and bassoonist Kayetan Cygański-Bolski turn to two composers long overshadowed by famous fathers: Irene Poldowski, Henryk Wieniawski’s daughter, and Roxanna Panufnik, daughter of Andrzej Panufnik. On the programme: Verlaine songs and Cantator & Amanda for bassoon and string quartet, among others.

item.title: PhilHERmonic: listen to women’s voices
item.description: October’s PhilHERmonic pairs concerts by outstanding women artists with talks about women in culture and women’s health. Two symphonic concerts (9 and 23 October, the second with conductor Aleksandra Melaniuk and violinist Noa Wildschut), sets by Dobrawa Czocher and Paulina Przybysz, and on 24 October the finale of the Pink Ribbon March and the Health Stage.

item.title: The Piano Fairy Tale: a musical show premieres on 11 October
item.description: The season’s first EDUphilharmonic event in the golden hall is a children’s show about Ludwik, a piano with 88 keys and a big dream who lands in Szczecin’s Konzerthaus, with a spider reporter called Krzyżyk at his side. With the Philharmonic orchestra and actors Agata Kolasińska and Aleks Joński; the composer, Mateusz Czarnowski, conducts.

item.title: The 2026/2027 season book is on sale
item.description: 256 pages on the whole season: concerts, the education programme for children, teens, adults and seniors, exhibitions, tours and practical ticket information. Every text in Polish and English, sewn hardcover. Price: 30 zł.

item.title: October at the Philharmonic
item.description: The month at a glance: the 79th season opening (2 and 3 October), the chamber project (NOT)Daughters, PhilHERmonic with Sul Yoon and Noa Wildschut, Dobrawa Czocher, Paulina Przybysz, Ennio Morricone through Mitch&Mitch (25 October), a Grammy-nominated guitar duo (28 October), Beethoven and Mozart with pianist Olga Zado (30 October) and the first Symphonic Monuments (31 October). Plus the Piano Fairy Tale premiere and a new exhibition season.

item.title: Beethoven, Chopin, Sibelius: how the 79th season begins
item.description: Preview of the opening concerts on 2 and 3 October: Beethoven’s Egmont overture, Chopin’s Piano Concerto No. 2 in F minor with Georgian pianist David Khrikuli, and Sibelius’s Symphony No. 2 in D major. The Philharmonic’s director, Przemysław Neumann, conducts.

item.title: Seniors’ Culture Weekend, 3–4 October
item.description: The Philharmonic joins the 13th edition of the Ministry of Culture’s nationwide campaign. On Saturday and Sunday, 3–4 October, 12:00–16:00, seniors can visit both our galleries for free: Łukasz Patelczyk’s paintings in Galeria Poziom 4 and a photo story about charcoal burning in the Bieszczady mountains in the Art.Room.

item.title: Box office and café on Wednesday, 23 September 2026
item.description: That day, because of an event run by an outside organiser, the box office works from the entrance vestibule, the building is closed to visitors and Symfonia Cafe is closed all day.

item.title: Jazz this season, starting with Paulina Przybysz
item.description: Four jazz nights in the symphony hall: Paulina Przybysz with Insides (19 October), the Borys Janczarski Ensemble with American trumpeter Larry Browne (1 February), the Scandinavian Art Ensemble with music around Tomasz Stańko (5 April), and for International Jazz Day, vibraphonist Bernard Maseli with our orchestra (30 April).

item.title: Events by outside promoters in October 2026
item.description: A list of October concerts for which the Philharmonic only rents out its hall, including Natalia Kukulska, SBB, Maleńczuk, SOYKA / GROTT Orkiestra and a charity concert by the Polish Doctors’ Orchestra. Tickets are sold by the promoters, not the Philharmonic box office; for purchases and refunds contact them directly.

item.title: Two artists, three works and the first PhilHERmonic concert
item.description: Preview of Morning in the City (9 October): Korean cellist Sul Yoon, a Queen Elisabeth Competition laureate, and German conductor Katharina Morin with the Philharmonic orchestra. On the programme: Haydn’s Symphony ‘Le Matin’, Tchaikovsky’s Rococo Variations and Vaughan Williams’s A London Symphony.

item.title: Box office and café on Friday, 18 September 2026
item.description: From 3 pm the box office works from the entrance vestibule and the building is closed to visitors. Symfonia Cafe is closed all day.

item.title: Women in Classical Music Meet Up 2026: the Philharmonic is an Honorary Partner
item.description: The third meet-up of women working in classical music takes place on 4–5 October at the Rother Mills in Bydgoszcz. Topics include working with concert halls, audience research, communication and career change. The Philharmonic’s director, Przemysław Neumann, joins the panel ‘What do concert halls need?’.

item.title: Every note has a story: Listening Academy with Jakub Stefek
item.description: Four talks of about half an hour by Dr Jakub Stefek before selected symphonic concerts: about the composers, how the pieces came about and the stories around them, no prior knowledge needed. They start at 6 pm in the chamber hall and are free with a ticket for that evening’s concert. The first one is on 6 November, before Power and Splendour.

item.title: The 2026/2027 exhibition season
item.description: This season’s theme in the Philharmonic galleries is Prześwit (a gap that lets the light through), curated again by Katarzyna Szeszycka. From 1 October: paintings by Łukasz Patelczyk and the Seidler-Kumor family’s photographs of charcoal burning in the Bieszczady; from 11 December, mountain photographs by our patron, Mieczysław Karłowicz; later on, Bartek Otocki, Slevin Aaron and Paweł Kula, among others.
